title: How to Calculate Your Cyber Security Jobs Salary: Hourly to Annual Guide
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary for cyber security jobs. Use our formula with a 38-hour week, tax, and super. Based on Fair Work and ABS data.
salarySummary: For a full-time cyber security role on a 38-hour week, the annual salary is your hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the formula to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. So annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $50 per hour gives $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How does the National Minimum Wage affect cyber security jobs salary?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for adults, or $33.05 per hour for casuals including 25% loading. Most cyber security roles pay well above this minimum, but award rates may apply if you are covered by an industry award such as the Professional Employees Award. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the annual salary figure?
faqs.a: No. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Our calculator shows your gross annual pay before super. The total cost to your employer is your gross pay plus super. For example, on a $98,800 salary, super adds about $11,856.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you are looking at **cyber security jobs salary** information, you have probably seen hourly rates advertised alongside annual packages. Converting between the two is straightforward, but you need to know the right assumptions. This guide explains the formula, the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, tax, and superannuation. We rely on data from the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office.

## The Formula: Hourly to Annual

The basic calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a standard full-time employee, we assume a 38‑hour week. That is the ordinary hours under most awards and the National Employment Standards. So if your hourly rate is $50, your annual gross pay is:

$50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800

If you work part‑time, use your actual weekly hours. For casual employees, the hourly rate already includes the 25% casual loading – do not add it again. Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you check a box to add casual loading on top of the base rate.

You can also think in fortnights: weekly pay × 2. For a $50‑per‑hour full‑timer, weekly pay is $1,900, so fortnightly pay is $3,800 before tax.

## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for adults. That works out to $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get $33.05 per hour, which includes the 25% casual loading.

Most cyber security roles pay above the minimum, but some entry‑level positions may be covered by an award. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award. For example, the Security Services Industry Award (MA000016) covers security officers, but cyber security analysts are more likely to fall under the Professional Employees Award or a specific enterprise agreement. Always check which award applies to your job.

Award rates include penalty rates for weekends, public holidays, and night shifts, as well as allowances. Our calculator does not include those – it assumes the same rate every hour. For a precise figure, use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool.

## Cyber Security Jobs Salary: What the Data Shows

The search results do not provide a specific **cyber security jobs salary** figure. However, the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show that full‑time adult ordinary‑time earnings are $2,083.70 per week. That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352 (× 52). Many cyber security roles – such as security analysts, penetration testers, and security architects – fall in or above this range.

For a more tailored estimate, look at advertised hourly rates for your role and experience level. Then apply the formula above. Remember that contractors often quote a rate that includes super and leave loading, while employees see a base rate plus super on top.

## Tax and Superannuation

Tax is deducted from your gross pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 + 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $98,800 salary, super adds $11,856. Your total cost to an employer is gross pay plus super.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, then estimates tax, Medicare, and super. The results are an estimate – they do not include penalty rates, allowances, salary sacrifice, or the Medicare levy surcharge. For a binding determination, consult your employer or a tax professional.

For more reference data, see our [reference tables](/data) on minimum wages, award rates, and average earnings. You can also read about [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for different scenarios.
